channel.title: albums on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in albums on Loud Legends

item.title: ROB HALFORD on JUDAS PRIEST’s Turbo Backlash: 'Everybody Wanted To Throw It In The Bin'
item.description: In a new interview with U.K.’s Planet Rock, Rob Halford spoke about JUDAS PRIEST’s upcoming headlining appearance at the 2026 edition of the Bloodstock Open Air festival.

item.title: STATIC-X Bassist TONY CAMPOS On 'Life-Changing' OZZFEST: 'Eternally Grateful' To OZZY And SHARON
item.description: STATIC-X bassist Tony Campos recently looked back on the band’s breakout opportunity on Ozzfest in 1999, recalling a memorable encounter with the Prince of Darkness himself, Ozzy Osbourne.

item.title: MAX CAVALERA Explains Why a Second NAILBOMB Album Will Never Happen
item.description: Max Cavalera has once again shot down the possibility of a second NAILBOMB studio album, maintaining that the project’s legacy is best preserved as a “cult” one-off.

item.title: Paul Stanley Reveals KISS’s Biggest Song of All Time: 'Massive Hit, Yet Unlike Anything We’d Done Before'
item.description: Paul Stanley isn’t hedging. He called “I Was Made for Lovin’ You” the biggest KISS song of all time, pointing to 1.3 billion Spotify streams and roughly 850,000 daily plays as of late August.

item.title: Ex-MUSHROOMHEAD Vocalist WAYLON REAVIS’s 'A KILLER’S CONFESSION' Announces 'VICTIM 2' Album Featuring a Surprising NIRVANA Cover
item.description: A Killer’s Confession, the band led by former Mushroomhead vocalist Waylon Reavis, is gearing up to release a new album titled Victim 2. It’s set to arrive on September 19 through MNRK Heavy.

item.title: HALESTORM Drops New Song 'RAIN YOUR BLOOD ON ME' From Upcoming Album 'EVEREST'
item.description: Halestorm has released a new single titled “Rain Your Blood On Me,” giving fans another preview of the band’s next studio album, Everest, due out August 8 through Atlantic Records (listen below).

item.title: DEFTONES Return With New Album PRIVATE MUSIC And First Single 'MY MIND IS A MOUNTAIN'; VIDEO
item.description: Deftones are officially back. The California alt-metal band has announced their new album, private music, and dropped its lead single, “my mind is a mountain,” along with a brand-new music video (watch below).

item.title: The AC/DC Album Fans LOVE to HATE Isn’t as BAD as You Remember
item.description: In the early 1980s, AC/DC was riding high. The back-to-back success of Highway to Hell (1979), Back in Black (1980), and For Those About to Rock (We Salute You) (1981) turned the band into a global powerhouse.

item.title: The Song That Annoyed JAMES HETFIELD, but METALLICA Covered Anyway: 'It Drove Me Nuts'
item.description: James Hetfield has built a career on intensity and control, but even he has moments where personal taste takes a back seat. One of those moments came in the late 1990s, when Metallica recorded “Turn the Page” for their 1998 cover album Garage Inc.

item.title: Megadeth Celebrates 40 Years of 'Killing Is My Business' With Limited Box Set
item.description: Megadeth is marking the 40th anniversary of its debut album with a special box set release. Titled Killing Is My Business… And Business Is Good!, the ultra-limited collection arrives October 17 and will be restricted to just 350 copies.

item.title: AC/DC Opens European Tour in Prague, Czech President Attends; VIDEOS
item.description: AC/DC launched the summer leg of their “Power Up” European tour Thursday night in Prague, Czech Republic. The concert took place at Letiště Praha Letňany and drew an estimated crowd of 60,000 people.

item.title: Metallica's KIRK HAMMETT Recalls Struggling With 'The Unforgiven': 'I Wasn't Prepared For It'
item.description: Metallica guitarist Kirk Hammett is known for writing some of the band’s most famous guitar parts, but not every one came easy. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, he opened up about the difficulties he faced while working on the solo for “The Unforgiven”, one of the standout tracks from the band’s 1991 self-titled release, often called “The Black Album.

item.title: The Lemonheads Drop New Single “In The Margin,” Share Details on First Album in Nearly 20 Years
item.description: After years of writing, drifting, and starting over, Evan Dando is back. The Lemonheads are set to release their first studio album in almost two decades, titled Love Chant, arriving October 24 via Fire Records.

item.title: The RUSH Album That Led to Fan Backlash, Internal Tension, and a Moment of Regret: 'It Wasn’t the Smartest Move'
item.description: Most bands with long careers eventually take a creative detour. Whether to keep things fresh or avoid burnout, they try something new. Sometimes it works. Sometimes it doesn’t.

item.title: The AC/DC album that FLOPPED HARDER Than Expected And Nearly Turned Into A FULL-BLOWN CRISIS
item.description: Back in Black is the album everyone knows. It’s the one that sold like crazy and turned AC/DC into a global powerhouse. But not every album had the same luck.

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. SHADOWS On Being Misunderstood: 'People Are Just Getting It Now'
item.description: M. Shadows isn’t mad. He’s just… already moved on. If Life Is But a Dream… finally makes sense to you in 2025, congrats on solving the puzzle.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Says Younger Fans Ignore METALLICA Classics: 'They're More Into the New Stuff'
item.description: Not every Metallica fan has Master of Puppets tattooed on their brain. According to Lars Ulrich, a surprising number of listeners are skipping the band’s old-school thrash masterpieces in favor of more recent material.

item.title: David Ellefson Breaks Down Megadeth’s Risk and Its Divisive Legacy
item.description: In 1999, Megadeth rolled the dice with Risk, a record that veered sharply away from the band’s thrash metal identity. For David Ellefson, the album remains, in his own words, “probably the most controversial album in the catalog.

item.title: Is Slipknot Releasing a New Album in 2025? Here’s What We Know So Far
item.description: Slipknot fans are eagerly awaiting news of the band’s next studio album following 2022’s The End, So Far. While a new record hasn’t been officially announced, the band members have dropped numerous hints in recent interviews about their plans.

item.title: Vogg Says Decapitated’s New Album is Halfway Done, But When Will It Drop?
item.description: OKAY, SO—Vogg, the guitar wizard of Decapitated, has somehow managed to write 50% of the band’s new album. Fifty. Percent. Not 49%. Not 51%. Exactly half. And he dropped this information like it was no big deal while floating on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise, which, if you don’t know, is basically a lawless, floating metal festival where dehydration, questionable decisions, and ear-shattering riffs collide on the high seas.

item.title: Killswitch Engage’s Mike D’Antonio Rejects A.I. Claims: "I Don’t Wanna Be Associated With It"
item.description: Another day, another internet conspiracy theory—this time, aimed at Killswitch Engage bassist and graphic designer Mike D’Antonio, who’s had to crawl out of the art cave he’s been living in for the past eight months just to tell people to shut the hell up about A.

item.title: The Callous Daoboys Announce New Album "I Don’t Want to See You in Heaven"
item.description: Let me set the scene for ya: It’s 2 AM, I’ve had too much coffee, and I’m staring at my laptop like it owes me money. Somewhere in Atlanta, The Callous Daoboys are probably plotting their next auditory crime, gearing up to unleash I Don’t Want to See You in Heaven on May 16 via MNRK Heavy.

item.title: Dave Mustaine Confirms Megadeth’s Album 17 Is Taking Shape—205 Songs Under Review
item.description: Alright folks, gather ‘round—Dave Mustaine has spoken. And when Dave speaks, metalheads listen… usually while arguing on the internet about which Megadeth lineup was best. (If you said “Super Collider era,” we need to talk.

item.title: Jon Oliva Says New Savatage Album is Nearly Complete—But Can He Ever Perform Again?
item.description: Twenty years. That’s how long it’s been since Savatage last did a proper tour. Two decades of silence, barring the occasional “We might do something soon” tease. Well, guess what?

item.title: Sharon den Adel Confirms Within Temptation’s Next Album Is Taking Shape: “We Have a Clear Vision”
item.description: So Within Temptation has a plan. Well, sort of. Sharon den Adel insists they “really have an idea what we wanna do next,” which sounds promising—until you realize that the band started with the intention of taking their sweet time, only to immediately flip-flop.

item.title: Mercyful Fate Begins Work on First Album Since 1999, With Instrumentals Complete and Lyrics Next on the Agenda
item.description: After 26 long years, the wait for new music from Mercyful Fate may finally be nearing an end. While whispers of a fresh release from King Diamond and the band have been circulating for a while, bassist Becky Baldwin recently provided an update that confirms things are moving forward.

item.title: Teemu Mäntysaari Discusses Progress on Megadeth's New Album
item.description: Megadeth’s next album? Already in motion. Ideas everywhere, so many good ones, it seems. Guitarist Teemu Mäntysaari, speaking with Megadeth Digital, paints a picture of a band creating across continents.

item.title: Slipknot's Look Outside Your Window Finally Set for 2025 Release
item.description: Slipknot’s Look Outside Your Window is like Bigfoot. Always talked about. Never seen. But now, after nearly 20 years of “soon, we swear,” the album might actually happen.

item.title: Jim Root Pushes for Slipknot’s "Look Outside Your Window" Release
item.description: The wait for Look Outside Your Window has dragged on so long, it’s practically become folklore at this point. A decade or more of teasing, false promises, and cryptic updates, and here we are, still empty-handed.

item.title: Linkin Park’s From Zero Debuts Globally at No. 1, Lands No. 2 in the U.S.
item.description: Linkin Park’s latest release, From Zero, has made waves globally, though not without its share of quirks. The album, featuring new vocalist Emily Armstrong, hasn’t escaped controversy—her ties to the Cult of Scientology and all the thetanic baggage that comes with it have kept the gossip wheels turning.

item.title: Slipknot’s Clown Talks Delays for 'Look Outside Your Window'
item.description: Back in 2024, Shawn “Clown” Crahan of Slipknot confidently announced that the long-teased *Look Outside Your Window* would finally see the light of day this year. Fast forward to November, and here we are: still no album.

item.title: Linkin Park Announces From Zero Listening Events Across U.S.
item.description: Linkin Park is at it again, boys and girls—this time with listening events scattered across over 100 U.S. record stores for their new album, From Zero. Scheduled for Saturday, November 9, these events give fans a sneak peek at the record before it officially hits shelves on Friday, November 15.

item.title: As I Lay Dying's Comeback Album Mysteriously Disappears From Streaming
item.description: Mysterious times for As I Lay Dying fans. The band’s 2019 comeback album, Shaped By Fire, has all but vanished from streaming platforms, and the silence around its absence just adds to the mystery.

item.title: KORN's Debut Album Turns 30: Jonathan Davis Reflects on the Band's Legacy
item.description: Friday, October 11, marked 30 years since KORN unleashed their self-titled debut album (listen below). To commemorate the occasion, Jonathan Davis popped up on social media to share the album cover along with a few nostalgic words: “I can’t believe you’re 30 years old.

item.title: Evanescence to Begin Recording New Album in November
item.description: Evanescence—masters of gothic drama and mid-2000s radio dominance—is gearing up to record their next album. When? November. (Mark your calendars, or don’t. Your call.) The news dropped during an interview with 89 A Rádio Rock at Rock In Rio, where the band is currently melting faces.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Announces Eighth Album 'Through Storms Ahead'
item.description: Two and a half decades and a pile of albums later, AS I LAY DYING is tossing another entry onto their discography stack. Their eighth studio album, “Through Storms Ahead”, hits shelves (or playlists, let’s be honest) on November 15, 2024, courtesy of Napalm Records.

item.title: Linkin Park is Back with a New Album and Unexpected Vocalist
item.description: Leave it to Linkin Park to make their return a three-ring circus. A flashy new album, a shiny logo, and a brand-new vocalist, Emily Armstrong, were all unveiled during a livestream that pulled over 100,000 viewers on YouTube and an extra 26,000 on Instagram.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING’s New Album Delayed: Tim Lambesis Explains Why
item.description: Tim Lambesis, AS I LAY DYING’s frontman, recently chatted on the Loaded Radio podcast about the band’s long-gestating new album. Apparently, the record’s been done for a while, but mixing has turned into a never-ending tug-of-war.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Finalizes New Record Deal for 2024 Album
item.description: When Tim Lambesis sat down with Jamey Jasta on the “The Jasta Show”, the HATEBREED frontman probably knew he’d get some juicy tidbits on AS I LAY DYING’s new material.

item.title: Brian Welch on Korn's New Album: “The Heaviest in Years”
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch is dropping those familiar lines again—“heaviest stuff in years,” you know the drill. It’s almost like there’s a secret musician handbook, and on page one, right under “never say your best days are behind you,” is this classic line.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Delays Album Completion Again; See Details
item.description: Here we are again, AS I LAY DYING has a new album brewing, but don’t hold your breath just yet. Vocalist Tim Lambesis, in an interview with Chaoszine, dished out the details, or at least as much as anyone could get from his roundabout explanations.

item.title: Metallica’s Classic Albums Return in Limited Colored Vinyl Reissues
item.description: Metallica’s bringing out the big guns with their upcoming reissue series, serving up their classic albums on colored vinyl as if you haven’t bought these a few times already.

item.title: As I Lay Dying Begins Recording New Album With Fresh Lineup
item.description: The wheels are turning again for As I Lay Dying, and Tim Lambesis, the band’s infamous frontman, has confirmed their new album is officially in progress. Speaking with Heavy New York, Lambesis revealed that the group’s latest lineup is pulling its weight in the studio.
